\begin{abstract}
Vision--language models (VLMs) such as Vintern-1B bring strong multimodal abilities to
Vietnamese. However, adapting them to a new Visual Question Answering (VQA) benchmark usually
requires fine-tuning on many high-resolution image tiles or training a new architecture. We
propose \textbf{ViBridge-VQA}, which improves Vintern-1B without updating any of its pre-trained
weights. From a single image view, the frozen decoder receives two kinds of visual tokens.
\emph{Global} tokens are produced from the \texttt{[CLS]} vector by a small trainable bridge.
\emph{Local} tokens come from Vintern-1B's own pre-aligned projector and are pooled to a budget
chosen as the knee of the accuracy--cost Pareto front. On the reasoning-oriented AutoViVQA
benchmark, ViBridge-VQA trains 1.35\% of the parameters and reaches 54.6 F1, comparable to the
fine-tuned Vintern-1B, with 36 times fewer visual tokens. Adding a lightweight decoder LoRA raises F1 to 58.2. Our analysis shows that reusing the pre-trained projector is more effective than learning a new connector. The
local tokens also complement decoder adaptation, and their gain carries over to three other
Vietnamese VQA datasets.

\keywords{Vietnamese Visual Question Answering \and Vision--Language Models \and
Parameter-Efficient Learning \and Visual Token Budget \and Generative VQA}
\end{abstract}
